standard.title: Develop performance skills for drama
standard.description: develop performance skills relevant to selected drama styles and/or forms
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use voice and movement to communicate in drama (AC9ADR6D01). They have not yet developed skills systematically through deliberate practice, applied style-specific conventions, or used improvisation to extend technique.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop vocal and physical performance skills relevant to selected drama styles and forms, using improvisation and deliberate practice to extend technique.

nodes.label: Developing vocal performance skills
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop vocal skills — projection, clarity, pace, pitch, dynamics, pause — with deliberate intent to communicate in drama
nodes.minimum_width: Develop at least one vocal quality (e.g. projection, pace, dynamics) through deliberate practice; describe what changed and how the improvement changes the drama
nodes.typical_width: Develop a range of vocal qualities through sustained practice; use control of pace, pitch, dynamics, pause and silence to communicate mood, character and meaning; document development using drama terminology
wider: Develop vocal qualities of projection, clarity and contrast through deliberate work on all dimensions — pace, pitch, dynamics, pause and silence — document how each element changes what the voice communicates
Investigate how voice is used in a specific drama style/form (e.g. physical theatre, verbatim theatre) — experiment with those vocal conventions and evaluate what they add
Experiment with vocalisation beyond speech — silence, breath, sound — and evaluate how these communicate differently from language alone

response_modes.reason: Vocal skill development — projection, clarity, dynamic range, controlled use of pause — is fundamentally a consolidation task. The skills develop through sustained deliberate practice with feedback, not through exposure to more dramatic contexts. Students who practise vocal control repeatedly across a unit build genuine vocal range; students who try different styles without sustained practice do not.

success_criteria: Develops at least one vocal quality with a clear communicative purpose
Describes what changed and how the improvement affects the drama
Uses drama terminology to describe vocal development

nodes.label: Developing physical performance skills
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop physical skills — movement, stillness, gesture, use of space — to communicate relationships, status and meaning in drama
nodes.minimum_width: Develop at least one physical skill (e.g. use of stillness, spatial relationship, gesture) with a clear communicative purpose; describe what the skill communicates
nodes.typical_width: Develop physical performance skills including movement, stillness, realistic and non-realistic movement; explore ways to transition between scenes; use physical skills to communicate status/power relationships
wider: Develop use of the body across realistic and non-realistic movement — evaluate how departing from realistic movement changes what can be communicated
Experiment with using physical skills to communicate status and power relationships — investigate how posture, proximity, eye contact and gesture convey social dynamics

Develop understanding of how respectful relationships and empathy are expressed physically — explore how body language can affirm or undermine the dignity of characters from diverse cultural backgrounds

response_modes.reason: Students commonly use physical skills by habit — making eye contact, standing upright — without reasoning through whether those choices serve the intended communication. Scaffolding the reasoning ('what am I trying to communicate about this relationship, what physical choices serve that, does the audience receive what I intend?') builds deliberate physical practice.

success_criteria: Develops at least one physical skill with a clear communicative purpose
Describes what the physical choice communicates about relationship, status or meaning
Physical choices are deliberate — not just habitual movement

nodes.label: Applying style-specific conventions through improvisation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can experiment with conventions associated with specific drama styles/forms using improvisation to develop technique
nodes.minimum_width: Experiment with at least one style-specific convention (e.g. flashback, aside, slow motion, chorus) through improvisation; describe what the convention achieves and how it shapes dramatic action
nodes.typical_width: Experiment with a range of style-specific conventions using improvisation; use insights from improvisation to interpret scripted scenes in the style; document how conventions heighten tension, sustain dramatic action or communicate meaning
wider: Use improvisation to explore techniques for heightening and releasing tension in a specific style — then apply insights to scripted scene interpretation
Experiment with multiple conventions in sequence — evaluate how each shapes dramatic action differently and what combinations produce strongest effect
Investigate conventions from a drama style distinct from own familiar experience — develop enough command of the conventions to use them with intentional rather than approximate effect

response_modes.reason: Students who only practise conventions in one style cannot develop genuine understanding of what conventions do — they may apply them mechanically without understanding their function. Experimenting with conventions across multiple styles, using improvisation to discover their effects, builds genuine understanding of how conventions shape dramatic action.

success_criteria: Experiments with at least one style-specific convention through improvisation
Describes what the convention achieves — not just names it
Uses improvisation as a genuine discovery process, not just practice
